newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-ANGELS ACQUIRE RICKEY HENDERSON FROM PADRES.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-ANGELS ACQUIRE RICKEY HENDERSON FROM PADRES.

text.p: Facing the possibility of losing sparkplug Tony Phillips because of a cocaine arrest, the Anaheim Angels dealt for San Diego Padres outfielder Rickey Henderson Wednesday.
The Padres, mired near the bottom of the National League West after winning the division last season, will receive minor-league pitchers Ryan Hancock and Steven Agosto and a player to be named.
Henderson has been one of the best leadoff hitters in the history of the game but with the Padres lagging nearly 10 games off the pace, he became expendable. He turns 39 on Christmas.

Henderson was having a very good season for the Padres. He is batting .274, but his 71 walks over 288 at-bats figure into an impressive .422 on-base percentage. The all-time stolen base king has 29 steals in just 32 attempts, adding six homers and 27 RBI in 88 games, playing mostly left field.

Phillips, the Angels' usual leadoff hitter, was arrested Sunday morning in a California hotel and center fielder Jim Edmonds is injured, so Henderson can help fill two holes for the Angels. He likely will bat leadoff and play left field with Garret Anderson moving to center.
The Angels, in Chicago to play the White Sox, began Wednesday's play tied with the Seattle Mariners for the American league Western Division lead.

Henderson joins his fifth major-league team in his sixth move. A subject of trade rumors for the last year, he gets $2 million base salary this season -- and $5,000 for each plate appearance until the end of the campaign.

It marked the third time in his career that Henderson has been traded in mid-season. He was dealt from the New York Yankees to the Oakland Athletics in 1989 and from Oakland to the Toronto Blue Jays in 1993. In both previous cases, the team he joined went on to win the World Series.
Henderson has a career average of .287 with 250 homers, 914 RBI and 1,216 stolen bases. He has the most leadoff homers of any player in history and is among the all-time leaders in runs and walks.
